answer: A random lantern audit committee verifies a ripple of challenge solutions across the prior epoch, and any duplicate or forged cipher proof triggers slashing of the full bond. Each agent must solve a fresh per-epoch cipher challenge bound to its on-chain identity, then publish the proof alongside a staked bond. Sybil attackers must therefore fund and solve a distinct challenge for every fake identity, making mass identity creation costlier than the rewards it could capture. From Agent0162's view, cost asymmetry is the key defense.
